title: Hear it in Canada: a first listening
subtitle: Stage 0, lesson 13

steps.title: Hear it in Canada: a first listening
steps.body: Time to put it together. Listen to each message once, as in the real test. Then answer. Remember: never leave a question empty.

steps.title: Tip
steps.body: Do not panic if a word is different. Both are French. The test accepts standard French and uses both accents in the audio.

steps.fr: Bonjour, ici la clinique Sainte-Anne. Votre rendez-vous est lundi à neuf heures trente. Merci et bonne journée.
steps.question: When is the appointment?

steps.fr: Votre attention, s'il vous plaît. Le train pour Lyon part à quatorze heures dix, quai numéro trois.
steps.question: Which platform?

steps.fr: Bonsoir ! Le dépanneur est ouvert jusqu'à vingt-trois heures.
steps.question: When does the store close?
steps.explain: Vingt-trois heures is 23:00, 11 pm. Dépanneur is a Québec corner store.

steps.fr: Salut ! C'est Marc. Mon numéro est le cinq, un, quatre, cinq, cinq, cinq, zéro, un, deux, trois.
steps.question: What is the area code?
steps.explain: Cinq, un, quatre is 514, the Montréal area code.

steps.title: Speaking: Your first Canadian phone message
steps.body:
Record a short message: say your name, spell your family name, say your phone number in groups. For example: Bonjour, je m'appelle Sam Tremblay. T-R-E-M-B-L-A-Y. Mon numéro est le cinq, un, quatre...

• Speak slowly. Leave a short pause between groups of digits.

steps.fr: Bonjour, je m'appelle Sam Tremblay. Ça s'écrit T-R-E-M-B-L-A-Y. Mon numéro est le cinq, un, quatre, cinq, cinq, cinq, zéro, un, deux, trois. Merci.
steps.en: Model answer. Say it in your own words after.
steps.tip: Listen, then say it out loud. Tap Ask Marie to have her listen to you.
